check.title: Check the surface
check.running: Reading every sector. This takes about as long as ripping the disc.
check.what: Counts the bytes the drive's error correction could not fix. A disc reads perfectly right up until it does not — this is what shows the decline while there is still time to copy it.
check.fromHistory: from the recorded history of this disc
check.liveC2: Counting the bytes the error correction could not fix, as it reads.
check.liveNoC2: This disc reports no error flags, so the scan is looking for sectors that will not read at all.
check.stripPartial: where the errors are so far; {pct}% of the disc read
check.stripWhole: where on the disc the errors are

key.direction: left is the middle of the disc, right is the outer edge
discs.title: Discs checked before
discs.note: Kept in the database, so a disc checked today can be compared with the same disc checked next year. A disc is recognised by its table of contents, not by its name.

burn.blocked: This disc cannot be written to.
burn.filterPlaceholder: Filter by name, firmware or architecture
burn.verify: read the disc back and check it

burn.hintChecks: Everything that can be checked is checked before the laser is switched on. Afterwards every sector is read back and compared with the image.
burn.archiveNote: This is an archive. The disc gets the files inside it, as a filesystem — not the archive file. Every one is read back off the disc afterwards and compared with what went on.

format.zip.name: Zip
format.zip.note: Opens anywhere without extra software. Compresses each file on its own, so it is the largest of these on a folder of many small files.
format.tar.name: Tar, uncompressed
format.tar.note: No compression at all, so it is written as fast as the disc reads. Right for a disc that is already compressed - photos, video, audio.
format.tar.gz.name: Tar + gzip
format.tar.gz.note: The usual choice. Compresses well and quickly, and every system can open it.
format.tar.bz2.name: Tar + bzip2
format.tar.bz2.note: Smaller than gzip and markedly slower. Worth it for text and for installer discs.
format.tar.xz.name: Tar + xz
format.tar.xz.note: The smallest of these, and the slowest by some way. Right when the archive is going to be kept for years rather than opened tomorrow.
format.iso.name: ISO 9660 image
format.iso.note: A disc rather than a file about one: it mounts anywhere and it can be burned as it is, so a folder taken off a disc can go straight back onto one. No compression, and the long names are kept twice over - in Joliet and in Rock Ridge - so they survive on Windows and on Unix alike.
cap.readRaw.can: read raw 2352-byte sectors, so audio tracks and exact disc images are possible
cap.readRaw.cannot: read raw sectors, so only 2048-byte data sectors can be ripped - no audio, no raw image
cap.readC2.can: report C2 error pointers, so a rip can say which bytes it is unsure of
cap.readC2.cannot: report C2 error pointers, so a rip cannot tell a clean sector from a guessed one
cap.accurateCDDA.can: return audio samples at the address asked for, so an audio rip needs no jitter correction
cap.accurateCDDA.cannot: guarantee audio samples land at the address asked for, so an audio rip may drift by a few samples between reads
cap.mode2Form2.can: read Mode 2 Form 2 sectors, as used by Video CD and photo discs
cap.mode2Form2.cannot: read Mode 2 Form 2 sectors, so Video CD and photo discs may rip short
cap.upc.can: read the disc's media catalogue number
cap.upc.cannot: read the disc's media catalogue number
cap.sessionAtOnce.can: burn a disc in one pass (session at once), which is what an exact image copy needs
cap.sessionAtOnce.cannot: burn session-at-once, so an image with its own layout cannot be written exactly
cap.testWrite.can: run a burn with the laser off as a rehearsal
cap.testWrite.cannot: rehearse a burn with the laser off
cap.burnProof.can: recover from a buffer underrun mid-burn
cap.burnProof.cannot: recover from a buffer underrun, so a slow source can ruin a disc
cap.eject.can: open and close its tray under software control
cap.eject.cannot: open its tray under software control
